edges.rationale: The executable matrix preserves and extends the existing documentary concept map.
Calendar geometry is a specialized branch of the Cosmos research ecosystem.
The repository documents the 13 by 20 calendar period.
Alignment drift is represented through angular correction.
Maya and Inca records seed a wider comparison without asserting equivalence.
The validation pipeline compares the cosmological model with data and adversary models.
Covariance and uncertainty discipline can be applied to alignment measurements.
Catalogue records can supply object-level observations when provenance classes are validated.
Validated celestial events may become temporal reference data for calendar studies.
ChipQuantum provides an executable toroidal-computation context, while the Cosmos node governs semantic traversal.
Two-cycle traversal is proposed as a research-navigation topology.
The ChipQuantum overview names a sqrt3 geometry matrix; exact implementation evidence remains repository-specific.
The geometric factor sqrt(3)/2 must remain distinct from cosmological coefficients such as 3/2.
A return-map module is a candidate test for recurrence and attractor claims.
Graph metrics can measure coverage, orphan nodes and attention-state balance.
The script converts documentary relationships into validated graph records.
No current derivation justifies importing the prime note into cosmological claims.
Null limits and inferior fits must remain part of the model record.
Non-matches and cultural differences must be preserved rather than forced into one pattern.
